A paired bound schematic materially clarifies the item’s potentially confusing left/right lcm terminology, greatest versus least bound directions, and the order exchange under reversal. This is a warranted expository addition under the expanded diagram scope, not a claim that the original TeX failed.

correction: Added final Remarks illustration of left divisibility bounds and their transport by reversal to right divisibility; retained all existing bytes as an exact prefix, including full frontmatter, title, statement and proof.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Fix a,b in the existing B_n^+; g=a meet_L b and j=a join_L b; d is any common left divisor and m any common left multiple. All twelve panel labels are these elements or their rho images, in the same positive braid monoid.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The theorem parts (a),(b) and steps 2.1,3.1 supply g,j. F1 and def-left-and-right-divisibility-for-positive-braids define the orders.

diagram_math_checks.relations: Exactly six upward left-panel arrows assert d <=_L g, g <=_L a, g <=_L b, a <=_L j, b <=_L j, j <=_L m.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The first arrow is greatestness of the common divisor in (b)/step 3.1; the middle four are common-divisor/common-multiple membership; the last is leastness in (a)/step 2.1. Arrows are non-strict; no distinctness, cover, incomparability, extra vertices, or exhaustiveness is asserted, including when n<=1.

diagram_math_checks.map: rho:B_n^+ -> B_n^+ is the involutive word-reversal anti-automorphism. The horizontal rho arrow indicates transport of panels, not an additional divisibility relation between b and rho(a).
diagram_math_checks.justification: F4, def-left-and-right-divisibility-for-positive-braids clause (iv), and lem-the-positive-braid-monoid-is-left-and-right-cancellative statement/step 2.1 establish rho(bc)=rho(c)rho(b). Thus x<=_L y iff rho(x)<=_R rho(y); arrow directions remain upward.

diagram_math_checks.relations: Exactly six upward right-panel arrows are the rho images of the six left relations. In particular rho(g)=rho(a) meet_R rho(b), and rho(j)=rho(a) join_R rho(b).
diagram_math_checks.justification: F4 is an order isomorphism between the two named orders, despite being an anti-automorphism of multiplication. Its bijectivity transports all common bounds and their greatestness/leastness, exactly as proof step 4.1; no equality of the two orders or of left/right operations on the original pair is claimed.

diagram_math_checks.proof: The existing rigorous six-step proof is byte-for-byte unchanged and remains independent of the illustration.
